overview: 94 official Group 1 Qs (2008–2024) – the largest geography block: world physical divisions (23), rocks and minerals (18), drainage (16), India's divisions and parks (10 each). 2008–2012 were mostly 'where is X / what is X' one-liners; 2023–24 use match lists (tiger reserves, AP sanctuaries, Koeppen types, geo-heritage), river/basin orderings and 3–5-statement items. AP-specific facts (ranges, minerals, sanctuaries, geology) appear almost every recent year.

possibility.angle: World physical divisions – mountains, plateaus, deserts, straits, borders
possibility.what_they_ask: which country/region a range, desert, valley or basin is in; between which seas/rivers a feature lies; highest peak of a continent; country neighbours and coastlines; area order of countries

possibility.angle: India's physical divisions – Himalaya, hills, coasts, extent
possibility.what_they_ask: hills between rivers (Satpura), Meghalaya/Purvanchal hills, coast names, Himalayan structure and duns, India's lat-long extent, state with most neighbours
which Eastern Ghats range a landmark sits on (Tirumala – Seshachalam), district size comparison
focus vs epicentre, plate collision behind Himalayan quakes; natural targets: seismic zones, landslide-prone belts

possibility.angle: Natural drainage – world, India, AP rivers and lakes
possibility.what_they_ask: river sources, tributary of which river, which city/dam on which river, sea a river drains into, north–south order of Punjab rivers, basin size order within India, rift lakes
Koeppen type → Indian area, Mediterranean features, month of dust storms
El Niño facts and effect on Indian rain, where rainfall variability is highest
sholas, sacred groves, taiga and steppe features, biodiversity maxima, per-capita forest

possibility.angle: National parks, tiger reserves, sanctuaries (India and AP)
possibility.what_they_ask: park → state, AP sanctuary → flagship species, components of a tiger reserve, MAB-listed biosphere reserves, AP coastal IBAs and birds
conditions of a soil type (peaty), active vs passive soil-forming factors

possibility.angle: Rocks and minerals – India and AP
possibility.what_they_ask: leading state for a mineral, AP mineral → district/basin, odd one out among coalfields, ore → metal, Vindhyan series, Dharwar rocks in AP, geo-heritage sites, crust composition

traps.trap: Moves a feature to the neighbouring zone
traps.spot: Statements placing duns, lakes or valleys 'between' two ranges or 'part of' a rift
traps.fix: Duns lie between Lesser Himalaya and Shiwaliks; Lake Victoria sits between the two rift arms, not in them
traps.pyq: 'Duns [...] between Greater and Lesser' false → I, II, III [group1-prelims-2024-paper1#104]; Lake Victoria in Rift false → I, II, III [group1-prelims-2024-paper1#101]

traps.trap: Pairs a lake or dam with the wrong river
traps.fix: Kolleru lies between the Godavari and Krishna deltas (fed by Budameru, Tammileru); Wular–Jhelum, Gobind Sagar–Sutlej, Ukai–Tapi

traps.spot: Basin or area orders where an international river is listed
traps.fix: Within India Brahmaputra's catchment is small; order after Ganga: Indus > Godavari > Krishna > Brahmaputra

traps.trap: Adds a wrong component to a true core
traps.spot: A reserve 'comprises X and Y' where one name belongs elsewhere
traps.fix: Satkosia TR = Satkosia Gorge + Baisipalli sanctuaries; Debrigarh is a separate sanctuary

traps.trap: Swaps the dry season of a climate type
traps.spot: Koeppen or Mediterranean statements on 'dry winter' vs 'dry summer'
traps.fix: Mediterranean (Cs) = dry hot summer, wet mild winter; Coromandel = As (dry summer); NE India = Cwg (dry winter)
traps.pyq: → I, II, IV not features [group1-prelims-2024-paper1#98]; Koeppen match → A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV [group1-prelims-2024-paper1#105]

traps.trap: Inserts a non-coal (or non-member) item in a homogeneous list
traps.spot: 'Not a coal field', 'not part of the Great Lakes', 'not MAB'
traps.fix: Mosabani is copper; Victoria is in Africa; non-MAB BRs: Cold Desert, Dibru-Saikhowa, Great Rann of Kutch, Manas, Seshachalam, Dihang-Dibang

traps.trap: Reverses the temperature range of a biome
traps.spot: 'narrow range of temperatures' for a high-latitude biome
traps.fix: Taiga has an extreme annual range; narrow range belongs to equatorial forests

traps.trap: Calls a passive soil factor active
traps.spot: Lists of soil-forming factors with 'active' in the stem
traps.fix: Active: climate, organisms; passive: parent material, relief, time

traps.spot: 'one-fourth of the crust is feldspar and quartz'
traps.fix: Feldspar alone is about half the crust; oxygen and silicon dominate

techniques.name: Mental-map ordering
techniques.how: For N→S or W→E orders, picture the map once and read it off; check only the adjacent pair that differs between options.
techniques.example: Punjab rivers N→S: Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej [...]; options differ on Ravi/Beas → Ravi is north → option 3 [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#118]

techniques.name: Flagship-species anchor for AP sanctuaries
techniques.how: Learn one flagship per AP sanctuary; in a match list fix the rarest pair first.
techniques.example: Rollapadu = Great Indian Bustard, Coringa = saltwater crocodile → only 'A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II' survives [group1-prelims-2024-paper1#110]

techniques.name: Habitat-fit elimination
techniques.how: For 'species not found in' items, ask whether the species' habitat (wetland, dry hill forest, coast) exists in that park.
techniques.example: Sri Venkateswara NP is dry hill forest (red sanders, Cycas beddomei, slender loris); wood stork is a wetland bird → option 1 [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#100]

techniques.name: AP geology by region
techniques.how: Tie each rock system to its AP area: Dharwar – Nellore/Chittoor schist belts; Cuddapah – Kadapa basin (uranium at Tummalapalle, barytes at Mangampet); Kurnool system – Kurnool; Gondwana – Godavari valley; Khondalite – Eastern Ghats.
techniques.example: Dharwar rocks → Chittoor and Nellore [group1-prelims-2024-paper1#109]; uranium → Kadapa Basin [group1-prelims-2017-paper1#141]

techniques.name: Source–tributary chain
techniques.how: For each major river keep source → main tributaries → mouth; a tributary question becomes a lookup.
techniques.example: Jayamangali is a Penna tributary (with Kunderu, Chitravati, Papaghni) → Pennar [group1-prelims-2010-reexam#1]; Krishna rises at Mahabaleshwar [group1-prelims-2012#55]

techniques.name: Coastline sweep
techniques.how: For 'which countries touch X ocean' trace the coast in order; flag the one country with only a different sea.
techniques.example: Pacific coast N→S: Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Chile; Venezuela faces only the Caribbean → I, III, IV, V [group1-prelims-2024-paper1#102]

confusions.remember: Palk is north of Adam's Bridge; from Nagercoil (south) you cross the Gulf of Mannar
Tarim between Kunlun and Tien Shan; Tsaidam between Kunlun and Altyn Tagh
Duns between Lesser Himalaya and Shiwalik; Kashmir between Great Himalaya and Pir Panjal
Focus is underground origin; maximum intensity at epicentre
Hardness vs quake intensity vs magnitude
Eastern Ghats ranges of AP each have a landmark
AP coast is not Coromandel or Konkan
Cs dry summer, Cw dry winter, Cf no dry season
Intense leaching in hot wet areas vs organic soil of heavy-rain humid areas with dense vegetation
Telineelapuram deaths were pelicans; Mycteria leucocephala is the painted stork
Great Indian Bustard vs Jerdon's courser
Singhbhum copper belt vs Gondwana coal

anchors: India: 3.28 million sq km, 2.4% of world area; 8°4′–37°6′ N, 68°7′–97°25′ E; 28 States + 8 UTs
Karnataka borders the most states among southern states
Punjab rivers N→S: Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej
Basins within India: Ganga > Indus > Godavari > Krishna > Brahmaputra
Pranhita – largest Godavari tributary by area
Krishna – Mahabaleshwar; Godavari – Trimbakeshwar; Jhelum – Verinag
Kolleru – between Godavari and Krishna deltas
AP – sole producer of apatite; Kadapa – asbestos, barytes, uranium (Tummalapalle)
Odisha – largest bauxite and manganese producer (in the asked years)
Ruby = Al₂O₃ with chromium; wolframite = tungsten ore
Crust: O > Si > Al > Fe; feldspar ≈ half the crust
18 Indian BRs, 12 in UNESCO MAB; non-MAB include Cold Desert, Dibru-Saikhowa, Great Rann of Kutch, Seshachalam
Sholas – Western Ghats high hills (Anaimalai, Palani, Nilgiri)
El Niño – warm water off Peru, weak Indian monsoon (e.g. 2014)
Geo-heritage: Lonar – Maharashtra; Akal – Rajasthan; Siwalik Fossil Park – HP; Nomira pillow lava – Odisha
checklist: Locate the feature on a mental map before reading options
Watch qualifiers: 'within India', 'among the following', 'in AP', 'presently'
For 'between X and Y' statements, check both bounding features
In 'not a member' lists, find the item from a different category or continent
For match lists, fix the rarest pair first and test the surviving codes
For AP items, tie each fact to its district/range/basin
For climate/biome statements, check which season is dry and how large the range is
